title: Damn thing works
author: Low-Yellow6950
selftext:
With the multiple stress testing, the trading bot. Finally achieved nearing 93% WR. I gave the bot only $100 to only work with live papertrading. 

I mainly learned all the technicalities from books I've read and, shockingly enough, Instagram algorithm traders. 

Everyone goes for the 4 to 6 figure of testing. But I do it for the common folk of people who can afford $100 - $500. Where the options are not that great and hard to find the right opportunities on making money.

comments.author: Ok_Map5721
comments.body:
Congrats on getting it running, that part is harder than people admit. A few honest notes though, because I've been burned by exactly this kind of screenshot myself.

14 trades on two dates is really two observations, not fourteen. Trades on the same day move together, so one good market day can produce 13 wins by itself. And since the dates were reused, the bot has already seen them.

Win rate on its own says very little. +$0.22 over 14 trades means the average winner is tiny, so one normal loser can wipe out the whole run. Average win vs average loss tells you much more.

Fees are the big one at $100. If each trade is around $100 notional, a typical taker fee is about 5 to 10 cents per round trip, so 14 trades can cost more than the $0.22 you made. Check whether the paper account charges real fees and spread.

What would actually convince you: run the exact same settings, no tweaks, on 100+ days the bot has never seen, with fees on. Then compare against random entries with the same holding time. If it still beats random after that, you've got something.

Not trying to rain on it. Small accounts are exactly where costs eat everything, so it's worth knowing early.

replies.author: Low-Yellow6950
replies.body:

replies.author: Ok_Map5721
replies.body:
fair enough, no commission helps a lot. one thing to watch though: zero commission doesn't mean zero cost. you still pay the spread every time you get in and out, and that's usually how commission-free brokers make their money. with 10% per trade that's about $10 a position, so $0.22 over 14 trades is roughly 0.15% per trade. on a lot of names the spread alone is close to that. easy way to check: compare your actual fill prices with the mid price at the moment you entered. if they're close, great, you've got a real cushion.

and yeah, today's market is a proper stress test. if it holds up through weeks like this, that tells you more than any backtest.

replies.author: Disastrous-Pie-6383
replies.body:
I agree 100% . I am building out my own system and what I noticed very quickly was I need as much data as I can possibly get. On my system once a trade is armed it looks for a specific entry. Once that number is hit the trade turns to triggered. From thee I have a T1 and T2 price for profit , as well as a cut price if the trade falls apart. I currently am tracking each trading day individually, to see if my setup works better on certain days . I also tracking how much the trade moves once I enter it , no matter if I hit T1,T2 or the cut. I also want to know the percentage it moved towards T1 , once I am in the trade bc I noticed some trades will actually hit my cut price before my T1 profit , but if you look at the amount or percentage they moved towards T1 sometimes the trade is actually a win. For example I have had a few times where on my chart the trade is a "loser" but it move 90%+ towards the T1 price. I also keep track of how long I am in each trade before hitting my T1, T2 or cut price bc I have also had trades be "winners" but moved so fast ( had one that was 7seconds ) I wouldn't have been able to get in and out of the trade before it fell apart.

So with that being said, build the system that you think will work and then watch it for a solid week or two and keep track of as much information as you can and then go over it manually and adjust.

Good luck !

replies.author: Ok_Map5721
replies.body:
that's a really good set of things to log, most people only record win/loss. the "how far it moved toward T1" number is basically MFE (max favorable excursion), and tracking it next to MAE (how far it went against you) is the cleanest way to choose targets and stops.

one trap I fell into with exactly this: you see a few losers that got 90% of the way to T1, you move T1 closer, and the last two weeks suddenly look great. but you've just fitted the target to those specific trades. what helped me: decide the change in writing, then judge it only on trades that happen after you made it.

same with splitting by weekday. with a week or two of data, each day has a handful of trades, so one day will always look best by luck. I'd wait for a few dozen trades per bucket before believing any of those splits.

and the 7-second winners are a great catch. if you can't realistically get filled on them, they shouldn't count in the results at all.

once you've run your tests for a while, I'd really like to see how it turned out. DM me if you're up for sharing, happy to go through the numbers together.

replies.author: Individual_Tip6170
replies.body: you can try breakeven or half sl (it will only activate when reaches 90% to TP) when trade comes up to 90% to TP so if it reverses it you will not loss your full SL

replies.author: Ok_Map5721
replies.body: good idea, and it's exactly the kind of rule the MFE log can test. the catch is it's not free: some trades that reach 90%, pull back a bit and then hit TP anyway would get scratched at breakeven instead. so it trades a few full losses for a few lost wins. with a log of how far each trade went in both directions, you can replay the rule on past trades and see which side is bigger. then lock it in and check it on new trades.

comments.author: AoideusWasBanned
comments.body:
With 13 wins out of 14 and +$0.22 total, the number I'd look at is the size of that one loss compared to the average win. ADX setups with tight take profits often win small many times and lose big once, so a 92% win rate can still turn negative after a few more trades.

  
On $100 the fees matter a lot too. A typical 0.1% per side is about 20 cents per round trip on the full balance, so make sure the backtest charged that on every one of the 14 trades, plus some slippage on entries.

  
If it still holds after costs over a few hundred trades on data you haven't touched, then it's worth getting excited.
